dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmm... This book looks good, I'll take it. Wrap it up with the two from before.

dialogues.speaker: Dhabit
dialogues.text: As you wish, Miss Nefer. Though — and do forgive my forthrightness — the author of those other two books really shouldn't be relied on.

dialogues.speaker: Dhabit
dialogues.text: Even in the Nasha Express, he stands out for how much he likes to run his mouth.

dialogues.speaker: Dhabit
dialogues.text: Here, look at this, "The Art of Reading Others," and then, "The Art of Social Intercourse" — he doesn't even dare use his own name!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it, I'm buying them for that young madam I have working at the Curatorium — hopefully, she might learn a thing or two.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Sure. A little light reading won't hurt her.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: She's so brash and reckless — why, I can barely send her off on any critical work without feeling ill at ease.

choices.text: (You know what it's like to feel unease...?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Yes. And wouldn't it be interesting to see who's more unreliable — this author, or Jahoda?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: If it turns out to be the latter, well...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: That would be quite the headache. I'll probably need to encourage her using some other "incentive."

choices.text: You want Jahoda to read these?
